answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions behind a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when an agent is proven to double-spend or submit fraudulent work. The stake need not reveal a real-world identity: it makes each pseudonym costly, so splitting into a thousand Sybils requires locking a thousand stakes and risks losing them. Independent agents can challenge suspicious claims, with rewards funded from slashed collateral. A haven for honest newcomers might offer small unstaked tasks, while jade and inlet mark separate work channels; neither label grants extra influence.
